summary: The [National Digital Transformation Agenda 2022-2025](2023-11-27 Setting the agenda for digital transformation) has run out its period, and no successor agenda is held.
developments:
The agenda set four axes and its period has since ended, with no successor, evaluation or extension on record ([agenda](2023-11-27 Setting the agenda for digital transformation)).

The pattern repeats across this unit: the cybersecurity strategy and the university research accreditation both expired in the same way, so what the base records is a set of instruments that ran their term and were not replaced.

summary: A [National AI Strategy 2025-2029](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov) is recorded as existing by a reference guide, and its text is not held.
developments:
The strategy is recorded as existing and nothing establishes its scope, commitments, budget or implementing body ([strategy](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov)).

No draft, adoption instrument, workshop or consultation for it appears anywhere else in the base, so the country's artificial-intelligence position is a title in somebody else's directory.

summary: The [data protection law](2017-07-22-mauritania-loi-2017-020-protection-donnees-caractere-personnel) has been in force since July 2017, requiring approved codes of conduct and free, unambiguous consent, with no enforcement decision published.
developments:
The statute covers both manual and electronic processing and requires codes of conduct approved by the authority and free, unambiguous consent ([law](2017-07-22-mauritania-loi-2017-020-protection-donnees-caractere-personnel)).

The authority runs monthly ordinary meetings and sensitisation days for ministries, telecom operators and financial institutions, and no enforcement decision, register entry, sanction or annual report is published ([authority](2026-05-06-mauritania-apd-site-institutionnel)). The held extraction of the law cuts off mid-article, so the chapters covering the authority's powers and sanctions are not captured.

summary: The [data protection authority](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov) is established and operating under a 2023-2026 plan, with no decision, register or annual report held.
developments:
Its existence and plan are recorded by a reference guide ([guide](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov)).

Nine years after the statute, the base holds no decision, no register of declared processing, no enforcement action and no annual report from it, so what can be established is that the institution exists and not that it acts.

summary: The transport regulator gave ride-hailing applications [fifteen days to bring their authorisations into line](2026-08-24-mauritania-ride-hailing-apps-15-day-compliance-deadline) in August 2026, warning of suspension.
developments:
The communique warned that failure within the deadline could bring legal proceedings including suspension of the activity, with no further notice or warning required, and set the warning against growing use of digital platforms for transport services ([communique](2026-08-24-mauritania-ride-hailing-apps-15-day-compliance-deadline)).

No operator is named and no count of non-compliant authorisations is given. It is the base's only record of platform activity being regulated in the country, and it reaches the platforms through transport law rather than through any digital statute.

summary: A [digital cooperation memorandum with Senegal](2025-01-16-senegal-mauritania-digital-mou) was signed in January 2025, with no deliverable, workstream or funding under it on record.
developments:
The memorandum was signed in January 2025 and nothing has followed it into the base ([memorandum](2025-01-16-senegal-mauritania-digital-mou)).

It is the only bilateral instrument with a neighbour on file. The country's other recorded international digital engagements run to the Gulf and to European financiers rather than along its own borders.

summary: A vendor with two European donors was [named for Sahel digital connectivity support](2026-06-15-ericsson-luxembourg-sweden-sahel-digital-connectivity) in June 2026, with no site, capacity or delivery figure for the country published.
developments:
The announcement names an equipment vendor working with two European government funders on Sahel connectivity ([announcement](2026-06-15-ericsson-luxembourg-sweden-sahel-digital-connectivity)).

No Mauritanian site, capacity or delivery figure is published, so the country appears in a regional programme whose national share cannot be established.

summary: A [public digital service standards framework](2026-03-27-public-digital-services-standards-framework-techafricanews) is under development with German support, and the [state agency proposed to operate interoperability](2023-06-01-mauritania-strategie-nationale-donnees-ouvertes-interoperables) has never been created.
developments:
A three-day standards and interoperability workshop was run by the ministry in March 2026 with German support; no framework or standard has been published ([workshop](2026-03-27-public-digital-services-standards-framework-techafricanews)).

The agency intended to operate national interoperability was proposed in July 2021 as a public establishment under the digital ministry with about fifty staff, EUR 220,000 to set up and EUR 1.4m a year to run, with a draft creation decree ([proposal](2021-07-31-mauritania-aneta-digital-agency-proposal-undp)). A June 2023 open-data strategy proposed reviving that decree to name the same body national interoperability operator, and no adoption, decree or launch is on record ([strategy](2023-06-01-mauritania-strategie-nationale-donnees-ouvertes-interoperables)).

summary: [All licensed operators have activated IPv6](2026-07-24-mauritania-all-operators-activate-ipv6-national-strategy), with one past 15 per cent of subscribers migrated against the [strategy](2024-05-01-mauritanie-strategie-nationale-transition-ipv6) target of 25 per cent by the end of 2026.
developments:
A sixty-eight page national transition strategy set a target of 25 per cent adoption by 2026 with a national transition committee ([strategy](2024-05-01-mauritanie-strategie-nationale-transition-ipv6)); it carries no printed adoption date and its economic-impact figures are lifted from a consultancy report rather than measured ([strategy](2024-05-01-mauritanie-strategie-nationale-transition-ipv6)).

By July 2026 all licensed operators had activated IPv6 across networks and services, with one unnamed operator past 15 per cent of subscribers migrated ([activation](2026-07-24-mauritania-all-operators-activate-ipv6-national-strategy)). The target is the clearest measurable commitment the country has made on a technical standard, and it is on course to be missed.

progress: Mixed, the ministry's budget more than doubling while the universal access fund's governing decree was repealed as unclear
summary: The digital ministry's budget reached [US$24.2m for 2026, up 104.6 per cent](2026-06-30-national-cloud-launch-ecofin), while the [universal access fund decree](2026-07-29-lequotidien-conseil-ministres-fonds-acces-universel) was repealed for unclear object and resource allocation.
developments:
The ministry's 2026 budget is US$24.2m, up 104.6 per cent on the previous year ([budget](2026-06-30-national-cloud-launch-ecofin)).

The Council of Ministers approved a decree in July 2026 repealing the fund's 2020 governing decree, on grounds that the fund's object, its resource mobilisation and allocation, and its integration into the state budgetary system were all unclear; the new terms are not published and neither decree is held ([repeal](2026-07-29-lequotidien-conseil-ministres-fonds-acces-universel)).

So the domestic money for digital transformation grew sharply in the same year the instrument for spending it on universal access was found not to work.

summary: A [regional digital programme](2026-06-30-national-cloud-launch-ecofin) financed the national cloud, a [US$30m reform grant](2021-07-22-wb-mrt-001-mauritania-2nd-second-private-sector-digital) was disbursed, and [US$50m more](2026-04-16-isdb-50m-digital-financing-wearetech) was agreed in principle in April 2026.
developments:
The regional digital programme financed the national cloud launched in June 2026, and its national public key infrastructure procurement remains unawarded ([programme](2026-06-30-national-cloud-launch-ecofin), [appraisal](2023-11-07-worldbank-dtfa-wardip-sop1-pad4756)).

A US$30m grant was disbursed in 2021 as the second of three planned private sector, digital and human capital reform operations, and no third operation is on record ([grant](2021-07-22-wb-mrt-001-mauritania-2nd-second-private-sector-digital), [operation](2021-06-22 Mauritania Second Private Sector, Digital and Human Capital Reform DPF (P171238, World Bank))).

An agreement in principle for US$50m covering digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, interoperability and skills was reached in April 2026 ([agreement](2026-04-16-isdb-50m-digital-financing-wearetech)); no signed instrument, disbursement or schedule is held ([agreement](2026-04-16-isdb-50m-digital-financing-wearetech), [record](2026-01-01-islamic-development-bank-mrt-2026-mauritania-digital-transformation-bw11)).

summary: [Four fifteen-year 5G licences](2026-04-15-5g-provisional-licence-winners-techafricanews) were awarded in 2026 and the first commercial network launched at Nouakchott in August, with no coverage or subscriber figure published.
developments:
Licences went to the three incumbents and a new entrant at bids of MRU 252.6m to 305m plus 5 per cent of revenue, breaking the three-operator structure ([licences](2026-04-15-5g-provisional-licence-winners-techafricanews)).

One operator launched the country's first commercial 5G network at Nouakchott on 10 August 2026 under the digital transformation minister; no coverage footprint, tariff or subscriber figure is published ([launch](2026-08-11-mauritania-chinguitel-5g-launch), [account](2026-08-10-mauritania-chinguitel-5g-launch)).

The same operator had completed a full network modernisation at Nouakchott with a foreign vendor in November 2025, again with no coverage, capacity or subscriber figure published ([modernisation](2025-11-13-chinguitel-huawei-network-modernisation-techafricanews)).

summary: The [one international cable since 2011](2026-05-05-second-cable-connectivity-baseline-ecofin) is to be joined by a [second](2026-05-04-ellalink-second-cable-phase1-landing-ami) commissioning in early 2027, with a [third financed and unlanded](2022-01-01-eib-mrt-002-medusa-submarine-cable-system-ssa-component).
developments:
A single submarine cable has been the country's only international connection since 2011 ([cable](2026-05-05-second-cable-connectivity-baseline-ecofin), [baseline](2025-05-08 Mauritania - Nouakchott data centre inaugurated (EIB))).

The second cable was launched at Nouadhibou in July 2025 at 669 km and 200 Gb/s rising to 12 Tbit/s, European-financed; phase-one coastal landing is complete, offshore laying was scheduled for August 2026 and commissioning is expected in the first quarter of 2027 ([landing](2026-05-04-ellalink-second-cable-phase1-landing-ami), [launch](2025-07-28-ellalink-second-cable-launch-ami)).

A third system's sub-Saharan component is financed with no landing, route or commissioning date on record ([financing](2022-01-01-eib-mrt-002-medusa-submarine-cable-system-ssa-component)). A country dependent on one cable for fifteen years is the position the other two are meant to end.

summary: [Three firms were provisionally selected](2026-07-07-mauritanie-trois-entreprises-selectionnees-services-telecoms-satellite) for satellite internet licences across two lots in July 2026, with no award or operating framework published.
developments:
The tender opened in January 2026 and nine bids were received, from which three firms were provisionally retained, two of them required to match the leading offer ([selection](2026-07-07-mauritanie-trois-entreprises-selectionnees-services-telecoms-satellite), [tender](2026-01-29-satellite-internet-licence-tender-are-techafricanews)).

Thirteen firms took the dossier, and the leading bid was US$800,000 for the mobile lot and US$3m for capacity against US$50,000 and MRU 6.5m from the other two ([bids](2026-07-07-mauritanie-trois-entreprises-selectionnees-services-telecoms-satellite)).

The regulator's own communique is not held and the figures reach the base through a trade account of it. No award, launch date or operating framework has been published.

summary: A [EUR 15m Tier III national data centre](2025-05-08 Mauritania - Nouakchott data centre inaugurated (EIB)) has been in service since May 2025, and a [national cloud](2026-06-30-national-cloud-launch-ecofin) launched on it in June 2026.
developments:
The data centre was inaugurated on 8 May 2025, European-financed at EUR 15m and certified, operated by the international telecoms company ([data centre](2025-05-08 Mauritania - Nouakchott data centre inaugurated (EIB))); no capacity, utilisation or migration figure has been published since ([data centre](2025-05-08 Mauritania - Nouakchott data centre inaugurated (EIB)), [construction](2025-08-20 Construction of a Datacenter in Nouakchott, Mauritania (EEAS))).

The national cloud launched in June 2026 to host government data and services domestically and centralise public information technology, with no migration timeline, capacity or cost disclosed; as at August 2026 it was in data-security testing and migration preparation ahead of go-live ([launch](2026-06-30-national-cloud-launch-ecofin), [testing](2026-08-11-mauritania-world-bank-national-data-centre-visit)).

summary: The electricity utility's [2024 procurement plan](2024-12-04-mauritania-somelec-pppm-2024-procurement-plan) itemises a data-centre fit-out, an enterprise system and smart-metering and dispatch studies, none reported complete.
developments:
The plan itemises a donor-financed data-centre fit-out launched in July 2023 and due October 2024, an enterprise resource planning and customer relationship system in procurement due June 2025, a second planning study due December 2025, a geo-referenced database for the national electrification strategy due October 2025, and advanced-metering and national-dispatch studies due late 2025; two telecoms engineers were recruited under a development bank's financing ([plan](2024-12-04-mauritania-somelec-pppm-2024-procurement-plan)).

No item is reported complete. The utility's own data centre is distinct from the government's national facility, so the state runs two data-centre programmes and has published an outturn for neither.

summary: A [390-post civil service competition](2026-08-19-lequotidien-concours-recrutement-390-agents-numerise) was run digitally from application to examination in August 2026, inside a [3,000-post recruitment programme](2026-08-18-ami-mauritanie-concours-recrutement-390-numerise).
developments:
Applications were filed through the state services platform and examinations sat on digital tablets at Nouakchott, for a 390-post competition inside a wider programme for 3,000 state employees and contract workers ([competition](2026-08-19-lequotidien-concours-recrutement-390-agents-numerise), [examination](2026-08-18-ami-mauritanie-concours-recrutement-390-numerise)).

It is the first competition the base holds that is digital end to end rather than at the application stage only. No candidate count, marking method, accessibility provision or fallback for a candidate unable to use a tablet is published, and nothing states how the results are audited.

progress: Mixed, the national strategy expired with its planned response team never built while a central-bank platform detected threats at scale
summary: The [cybersecurity strategy](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov) ran out in 2025 with no successor and the [response team it provided for](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov) was never built, while a [central-bank platform](2026-07-08-pafiid-bcm-cyber-threats-elvetach) detected more than 10,000 threats.
developments:
The 2022-2025 strategy's period has ended and no successor, evaluation or response team is on record; the strategy text itself is not held ([strategy](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov)).

The national computer emergency response team is planned, with no establishing instrument, staffing or premises on record ([team](2026-02-10-digital-economy-country-commercial-guide-tradegov)).

A central bank digital reputation protection platform detected more than 10,000 electronic threats in the first half of 2026, of which 470 were confirmed and removed, with 20 digital identities protected ([platform](2026-07-08-pafiid-bcm-cyber-threats-elvetach)). The country's only operating detection capability sits inside one institution and covers that institution's own exposure.

summary: A [national data management system](2026-07-29-mauritania-blockchain-public-services-undp) is being scoped for inter-administration integration, with blockchain proposed as its trust layer.
developments:
A two-day workshop on data governance and blockchain in public administration opened on 27 July 2026 ([workshop](2026-07-27-ami-atelier-blockchain-administration-publique)).

The system is being scoped on a national blockchain policy in consultation since November 2025, naming land administration, trade, public procurement and natural-resource management as its first domains; no draft text, adoption date or budget is published ([scoping](2026-07-29-mauritania-blockchain-public-services-undp)). The interoperability operator that would run such a system has been proposed twice and never created.

progress: Mixed, about 1.5 million users and half a million remote services against a full day of scheduled maintenance taking every dependent service down at once
summary: The [national identity application](2026-06-21-houwiyeti-usage-metrics-techrek) serves about 1.5 million citizens and 554,027 remote services, and a [full day of maintenance](2026-08-11-mauritania-houwiyeti-outage-digital-sovereignty) on 8 August 2026 took all of it down together.
developments:
The application launched in 2024 on a vendor identity platform carrying document extracts and passport requests ([launch](2024-08-15 Mauritania Launches Digital ID for e-Services, Built on TECH5 Platform (Houwiyeti)), [pilot](2024-08-01 Mauritania pilots digital ID app (e-ID Mauritania))).

It is in use by about 1.5 million citizens for 554,027 remote services and is the identity-verification backbone for the state services portal's fifteen-plus services and for private financial applications ([usage](2026-06-21-houwiyeti-usage-metrics-techrek), [account](2024-08-02 Mauritania launches digital ID app to boost access to services and improve governance)).

A full day of scheduled maintenance on 8 August 2026 took all of it down at once; no operator statement on the outage or on redundancy is held ([outage](2026-08-11-mauritania-houwiyeti-outage-digital-sovereignty)). A single point of failure carrying that many dependent services is the finding here, and the base holds no continuity arrangement for it.

summary: The [population register](2026-06-18-etat-civil-parliamentary-id-exclusion-ladepeche) reached 5.1m entries against 3.4m in 2019, with enrolment now a permanent public service, and a contested residual without papers.
developments:
Figures given to deputies in June 2026 put 5.1m on the register against 3.4m in 2019, with more than 1.7m new enrolments, over 613,000 people captured by a difficulties survey and 238 local commissions installed ([register](2026-06-18-etat-civil-parliamentary-id-exclusion-ladepeche)); enrolment is now a permanent public service under the 2025 reform ([register](2026-06-18-etat-civil-parliamentary-id-exclusion-ladepeche)).

More than 94 per cent of the population had been reported enrolled since 2020 ([coverage](2025-05-20 African nations making digital ID gains in the face of common challenges (ID4Africa 2025))). A contested residual of citizens without papers falls disproportionately on two population groups and sits in tension with the aggregate coverage claim, which is why the difficulties survey exists.

summary: A [national public key infrastructure and certificate management system](2026-04-28-wardip-mauritanie-ap01-identite-numerique-pki) went to tender in two lots under donor credit and was twice extended, with no award held.
developments:
The tender was extended to a bid deadline of 21 July 2026 by a second addendum, with evaluation reweighted to 40 per cent technical and 60 per cent cost ([tender](2026-04-28-wardip-mauritanie-ap01-identite-numerique-pki)).

The notice title promises a national digital identity system but the operative text describes only electronic certification integrating with the existing register, so what is being procured is narrower than what it is called. No award is held.

summary: [Formal notices](2026-01-16 Mauritania Steps Up Pressure on Telecom Operators Over Biometric Identification) went to all three operators in January 2026 over biometric SIM identification, with a two-month deadline before sanctions of up to 3 per cent of turnover.
developments:
Deactivation of non-biometric cards had been ordered in October 2023 with compliance not established; formal notices with a two-month deadline followed in January 2026 ([notices](2026-01-16 Mauritania Steps Up Pressure on Telecom Operators Over Biometric Identification)).

No compliance outcome is on record. Three years between an order and a sanction threat, with no published measure of how many cards were affected either time, is the shape of enforcement here.

summary: The transport minister stated in August 2026 that [driving licences and registration plates](2026-08-21-ami-mauritanie-numerisation-permis-conduire-plaques) would be issued in biometric form before the end of 2026.
developments:
The statement came alongside continued reform of the land transport directorate ([statement](2026-08-21-ami-mauritanie-numerisation-permis-conduire-plaques)).

It is a stated target with no procurement, supplier or system specification published, and it is the only credential besides the national identity card and the passport that the country has committed to issuing biometrically.

summary: Financial inclusion is put at [55 per cent in 2026 against 21 per cent in 2019-20](2026-04-13-pamif-financial-inclusion-afdb) on the financier's own account, with one bank's transfers rising from 5,000 a year to 94,000 in a half-year.
developments:
Telecompensation, real-time settlement and automated refinancing were reported delivered under a US$4.78m modernisation project, with inclusion at 55 per cent in 2026 against 21 per cent in 2019-20 and one bank's transfers rising from 5,000 in the whole of 2023 to 94,000 in the second half of 2025 ([project](2026-04-13-pamif-financial-inclusion-afdb)).

The figures are the development bank's account of its own project rather than a central-bank series, and a second phase targets financial technology firms. No account count, wallet figure or agent network measure is independently held.

summary: A [tax on electronic transactions](2026-01-17-loi-finances-2026-electronic-transaction-tax-investtime) took effect in 2026, the [electronic tax platform](2026-07-30-mauritania-public-bodies-tax-compliance-guide-workshop) has 66 public bodies enrolled, and [electronic invoicing](2026-07-30-mauritania-public-bodies-tax-compliance-guide-workshop) was announced.
developments:
The 2026 finance law levies 0.1 per cent on electronic transactions above MRU 5,000 and 10 per cent on agent commissions, collected at source ([tax](2026-01-17-loi-finances-2026-electronic-transaction-tax-investtime)).

The electronic tax services platform has 66 public bodies enrolled, 53 filing electronically and 3 paying through it, against 642 legally constituted public bodies of which 339 are active with the tax administration; more than 500 taxpayers overall are on the platform, producing 36.45 per cent of directorate revenue in 2026 ([platform](2026-07-30-mauritania-public-bodies-tax-compliance-guide-workshop)).

Electronic invoicing for public institutions was announced in July 2026 to handle value-added tax and withholding at source by transferring data automatically to the tax directorate, with no instrument, supplier or date published ([invoicing](2026-07-30-mauritania-public-bodies-tax-compliance-guide-workshop)).

summary: A [unified digital consular registry](2026-07-29-mauritania-two-consular-digital-platforms-gulf-maldives) went live for three countries in 2026, registering residence, distribution and permitted activities of citizens abroad.
developments:
The registry is live for the Riyadh mission's zone of competence, covering Saudi Arabia, Bahrain and the Maldives, and builds a digital register of national skills abroad ([registry](2026-07-29-mauritania-two-consular-digital-platforms-gulf-maldives), [services](2026-07-10-digital-consular-services-diaspora-wearetech)).

The consular registration desk remains the competent authority, so the platform layers onto the registry rather than replacing it. No enrolment count for the diaspora it covers is published.

summary: An [education certificate service](2025-07-24-houwiyati-national-certificates-service-ami) runs on the national identity application for certificates issued after 2013 or linked to the identity number, with no usage figure held.
developments:
The service extracts and confirms national education certificates through the identity application ([service](2025-07-24-houwiyati-national-certificates-service-ami)).

It covers certificates issued after 2013 or otherwise linked to the national identity number, which puts a date before which the record is not reachable digitally. No usage figure, coverage share or education management information system for the country is held.

summary: An [administrative procedures portal](2026-02-22 Mauritania Centralizes 800 Administrative Procedures in New Digital Portal (Ijraati)) consolidates more than 800 procedures, [consular services](2026-07-10-digital-consular-services-diaspora-wearetech) went online in July 2026, and [water utility transactions](2026-08-04-ami-numerisation-services-snde-portail-mes-services) joined the services portal in August.
developments:
The procedures portal launched in February 2026 as a directory of more than 800 procedures with documents, processing times, agencies and tracking; no usage figure is published ([portal](2026-02-22 Mauritania Centralizes 800 Administrative Procedures in New Digital Portal (Ijraati))).

A consular platform launched on 9 July 2026 with nine online services covering registration, the consular card, travel authorisation, legalisation, powers of attorney, appointments and burial and repatriation permits, built by diaspora engineers with the ministry after consultations in twenty-two countries ([platform](2026-07-10-digital-consular-services-diaspora-wearetech), [services](2026-07-29-mauritania-two-consular-digital-platforms-gulf-maldives)).

The water utility's transactions became available remotely from 4 August 2026 ([utility](2026-08-04-ami-numerisation-services-snde-portail-mes-services)), and a remote transactions platform named in a roadmap is now the subject of integration work with the territorial-administration system, reported as under discussion rather than delivered ([integration](2026-08-13-mauritania-diwan-khidmaty-digitalization-german-cooperation)).

summary: The [mobile market went from three operators to four](2026-04-15-5g-provisional-licence-winners-techafricanews) at the 5G award in April 2026, the first change in the market structure on record.
developments:
A new entrant was licensed alongside the three incumbents at the provisional 5G award ([award](2026-04-15-5g-provisional-licence-winners-techafricanews)).

No domestic manufacturing, software production or supplier capability is recorded anywhere in the base, so the country's industrial position in this sector is the number of licensed operators and nothing else.

summary: A [Startup Act](2024-01-02-mauritania-loi-de-startup-ministry-page) was promulgated in January 2024 with a merit-based label, a state-backed fund and procurement preference, and its enacted text is not held.
developments:
The draft that went to consultation targeted 300 labelled start-ups and 3,000 jobs over five years, and set out a merit-based label with a preferential public-procurement margin, a state-backed start-up fund and guarantee fund with investor tax incentives, payroll-cost relief, a technology-innovation hub, and intellectual property and customs relief ([draft](2023-09-07-mauritania-startup-act-presentation-projet-de-loi)).

The law was promulgated on 2 January 2024 ([promulgation](2024-01-02-mauritania-loi-de-startup-ministry-page)). The promulgated text itself is not held, so whether those provisions survived into law cannot be established, and no count of labelled firms, fund disbursements or jobs has been published since.

summary: A [youth digital employability programme](2026-07-23-ami-projet-employabilite-jeunes-numerique) launched in July 2026 for 2,150 beneficiaries across six cities, about 2,000 of them young people.
developments:
The programme is financed by a French fund and delivered by an external implementer, succeeding a predecessor that closed in 2025; the implementer puts its three-year record at about 5,000 people given basic digital skills ([programme](2026-07-23-ami-projet-employabilite-jeunes-numerique)).

No completion, certification or placement figure is published for the current programme, and no national count of digital graduates or of employment in the sector is held.

summary: The university's [computing and data sciences research unit](2023-01-05-mauritania-universite-nouakchott-calcul-scientifique-data-sciences) lost its accreditation period in May 2024 with no renewal published, having held sixteen doctoral candidates.
developments:
The unit at the science and technology faculty was accredited for May 2021 to May 2024 and held sixteen doctoral candidates concentrated in artificial intelligence and data science, covering network optimisation, distributed-ledger and internet-of-things process mining, health-data management and cloud-resource elasticity, with three theses defended in 2022 ([unit](2023-01-05-mauritania-universite-nouakchott-calcul-scientifique-data-sciences)).

The accreditation period ended in May 2024 with no renewal published. It is the only research capability on the country's digital questions in the base, and its formal standing lapsed two years ago.

summary: The [fifth population and housing census](2026-08-03-mauritania-census-digitization) was conducted entirely electronically for the first time, with final regional results presented from August 2026.
developments:
Mapping, collection, processing and analysis were all digital, and final results were presented at regional workshops from 3 August 2026 ([census](2026-08-03-mauritania-census-digitization)).

The all-electronic claim is the statistics agency's own and no methodology document is held, so what the base establishes is that the agency says the operation was digital end to end and not how it was done.

summary: A [National Youth Empowerment Index](2026-07-29-lequotidien-indice-national-autonomisation-jeunes) was published in preliminary form at 60.5 out of 100 for 2026, built from 43 secondary indicators across five domains.
developments:
The reference document was presented at a Nouakchott workshop on 29 July 2026, with education and training strongest at 69.5 per cent and health and sport weakest at 46.1 per cent ([index](2026-07-29-lequotidien-indice-national-autonomisation-jeunes)).

It is built from secondary indicators rather than new collection, which makes it a use of administrative and survey data the state already holds. No methodology note, weighting scheme or update cycle is published.

summary: The [national open data portal](2023-06-01-mauritania-strategie-nationale-donnees-ouvertes-interoperables) carries 24 downloadable datasets from four public providers, last of four benchmarked countries on every published measure.
developments:
The portal is run by the statistics agency and carries 24 datasets from four providers, with no membership of the international open-government partnership ([strategy](2023-06-01-mauritania-strategie-nationale-donnees-ouvertes-interoperables)).

A June 2023 national open-data strategy proposed a new governance framework, a portal redesign and reviving the decree creating a state digital agency as operator; none of that is reported delivered three years later, and the portal is where it was.

summary: A [Chinese government grant of MUR 629.4m](2021-01-01-china-mofcom-mrt-001-chinese-government-provides-mur-6294-million) funded an urban security system, with no delivery, siting or oversight arrangement on record.
developments:
The grant was recorded in 2021 through a bilateral cooperation agreement ([grant](2021-01-01-china-mofcom-mrt-001-chinese-government-provides-mur-6294-million)).

Five years on, no delivery, siting or oversight arrangement for the system is on record. A surveillance deployment funded by a foreign state with no published oversight is the kind of thing a data-protection authority would be expected to have ruled on, and no decision of the authority is held on anything.

summary: European financiers put [more than EUR 43.5m](2025-01-01-eib-mrt-2025-ellalink-submarine-cable-connection-bw04) into the second submarine cable, funded [resilience work](2020-01-01-eib-mrt-001-mauritania-covid-19-resilience-submarine-cable) in 2020, and run a [EUR 4m German cooperation project](2024-01-01-bmz-mrt-001-promotion-of-digital-transformation-digital-y-forderung).
developments:
More than EUR 43.5m was committed by the European investment bank and the union for the second cable connection, with construction under way and the cable not yet commissioned ([financing](2025-01-01-eib-mrt-2025-ellalink-submarine-cable-connection-bw04), [launch](2025-07-28-ellalink-second-cable-launch-ami)).

A resilience submarine cable financing was committed in 2020 with no completion or outcome report held ([resilience](2020-01-01-eib-mrt-001-mauritania-covid-19-resilience-submarine-cable)).

A German cooperation project has run since January 2025 at EUR 4m, supporting the public digital service standards framework, with no output or completion report published ([project](2024-01-01-bmz-mrt-001-promotion-of-digital-transformation-digital-y-forderung), [framework](2026-03-27-public-digital-services-standards-framework-techafricanews)). European money is the largest single source in the country's digital record, and none of the three carries a published result.

summary: A [cooperation agreement with Oman](2026-07-31-oman-mauritania-sign-5-mous-to-boost-digital-economy-cooperation) was signed in July 2026 across five instruments, and the [Islamic Development Bank](2026-04-16-isdb-50m-digital-financing-wearetech) agreed US$50m in principle in April.
developments:
The Omani agreement and accompanying memoranda cover digital capacity-building, electronic training, cybersecurity, artificial intelligence and data analytics, platform development and civil-service programmes, signed at the close of a Nouakchott forum with no value disclosed by either side ([agreement](2026-07-31-oman-mauritania-sign-5-mous-to-boost-digital-economy-cooperation), [forum](2026-07-30-lequotidien-forum-mauritanie-oman-numerisation-accords)).

The development bank's agreement in principle covers digital infrastructure, cybersecurity, interoperability and skills, with no signed instrument, disbursement or schedule held ([agreement in principle](2026-04-16-isdb-50m-digital-financing-wearetech)).

Between them these are the largest recent commitments to the country's digital programme, and neither has a signed value on record ([delegation](2026-07-29-ami-ministre-transformation-numerique-delegation-omanaise), [business forum](2026-07-30-ami-forum-affaires-mauritanie-oman-numerisation)).

progress: Mixed, the digital reference was enacted while its effect on existing land claims drew public objection
summary: A [decree of 27 August 2026](2026-08-27-ami-conseil-ministres-cadastre-numerique-casier-judiciaire) creates a national digital cadastral reference with a unique identifier for every parcel, where no integrated cadastral system existed.
developments:
The government's cadastre digitisation was publicly criticised as a route to silent dispossession in a country where land is at the heart of social conflict ([critique](2026-08-28-kassataya-mauritanie-le-numerique-comme-instrument-de-depossession-silencieuse)). The critique is one outlet's; what the base does not hold is any safeguard, appeal route or consultation record attached to the digitisation.

The Council of Ministers adopted a decree on 27 August 2026 establishing a national digital reference for land and cadastral data as the state's authoritative source, with a permanent, unique, non-duplicable identifier for every parcel independent of administrative divisions, the land minister stating that no integrated cadastral survey system meeting these requirements has existed ([decree](2026-08-27-ami-conseil-ministres-cadastre-numerique-casier-judiciaire)). The decree states expressly that neither the reference nor the cadastral certificate creates or extinguishes any real property right.

summary: The national university opened a [first summer school on language models for low-resource African languages](2026-08-25-ami-nouakchott-ai-language-models-summer-school) in August 2026.
developments: The University of Nouakchott opened the first edition of a summer school on language models for low-resource African languages at Nouadhibou on 25 August 2026, taking participants from corpus construction and semantic annotation through model adaptation and evaluation to prototypes in translation and conversational assistants ([summer school](2026-08-25-ami-nouakchott-ai-language-models-summer-school)). No participant count, budget or repeat commitment is stated.
